bottleneck: Therapeutic mRNA degrades within hours to days, requiring repeated dosing or continuous expression systems for chronic conditions. Current LNP delivery concentrates in the liver, leaving most tissues unreachable, and repeated LNP dosing provokes immune responses against the carrier itself. The transient, liver-centric profile that made mRNA vaccines work limits mRNA as a general medicine: protein-replacement therapy needs months of expression in specific tissues, which the platform cannot deliver.
current_state: Self-amplifying RNA extends duration modestly; extrahepatic LNP targeting is early-stage. Chronic mRNA therapy for non-liver diseases remains impractical.

sources.title: Architecting the Future of Health: From Code to Cure

title: mRNA therapies too transient and liver-locked
why_it_blocks: mRNA could treat any protein deficiency, but only if it lasts and reaches the right tissue. Without durable, targeted delivery, mRNA medicine stays confined to vaccines and liver targets while its broader promise waits.
